subtopic: Deciding what to do with pocket money
subtype: Approach: saving for a specific goal [Action]
passage: The football in the shop window cost four hundred rupees. Kamal received fifty a week. He borrowed a pencil and did the sum on the back of his hand: eight weeks. He drew eight boxes on a chart above his bed and coloured one at the end of every week. On Fridays at the canteen, when the chips smelled so good, Kamal walked past with his hands in his pockets. His sister Aparna teased him. "Is your football made of chips?" In the eighth week he counted his coins into the shopkeeper's palm, and the ball rolled into his arms.

qa.q: How many weeks did Kamal need to save?
What was Kamal feeling as he walked past the chips?
qa.a: Tempted but determined, since he kept his hands in his pockets and kept the football in mind.

qa.q: What could Kamal add to his plan for a surprise expense, and why?
qa.a: He could add a spare box or earn a little by helping at home, so one unexpected cost does not wreck the eight weeks.

qa.q: How does Aparna see Kamal's saving?
qa.a: Aparna finds it funny enough to tease him, though she seems to notice how seriously he keeps to it.

grounding: A boy works out how many weeks of pocket money a football needs, marks a chart and skips canteen chips.
